newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean unions threaten public service strikes.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean unions threaten public service strikes.

text.p: South Korea's most militant union body on Wednesday threatened an all-out strike by public sector workers unless the government scraps a new labour law by midnight next Tuesday.

"Subways, telecommunication companies, mints, freight services, newspapers and everyone else not on strike now will start industrial action on January 15 unless the government revokes the law," Kwon Young-kil, president of the Korean Confederation of Trade Unions, told reporters.
"To solve the current pressing problems in a reasonable way, the Korean Confederation is formally proposing a meeting with President Kim Young-sam," Kwon said.
President Kim on Tuesday made clear the government would not back down and argued the new labour law, which makes the labour market more flexible, was needed to bring down industrial costs.
Kim also ruled out a meeting with opposition parties to discuss the crisis.
Kwon said the confederation would join forces with all other labour groups, including the dominant Federation of Korean Trade Unions, from next Monday.
